_comment: 🎚️ The config state lane of `s.animate.presentation`'s editor (✏️editor/🎚️config): its mutation vocabulary `PresentationConfigMutation` over `PresentationConfig`, measured by the plugin bridge on the surface coordinate, claimed by `../../🧪️tests/🎚️mutate-animate-presentation-1-any-editor-config` and backed by one committed vector per declared outcome class.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: `PresentationConfigMutation` is the config state lane of `s.animate.presentation`'s ✏️editor/🎚️config surface: it holds the engagement input text of the presentation editor. This is this repository's own editor state record, not a published format, so no third party implements it. What is under test is that each kind (`set-engagement-input`) changes exactly its own part of `PresentationConfig`, that a kind declaring `no-op` leaves a record that already holds its value untouched with a warned `mutation.no-op`, and that every kind's computed inverse, read off the pre-mutation record, restores it exactly. Confidence comes from one committed, handcrafted (before, mutation, after, diff, outcome) vector per kind and declared outcome class under `../🧫️fixtures/`, exercised end to end through the production dispatch bridge, and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property.

candidatesConsidered.reason: A persisted key-value store for desktop settings; it has no model of this surface's typed config record, its per-kind setters, their no-op guard or the inverse each kind computes.
Loads and stores a whole configuration struct on disk; it defines no typed config mutations and neither their no-op nor their inverse behaviour.

referenceSurvey.whyNoneQualifies: `PresentationConfig` is a state record defined by this repository with its own typed mutation vocabulary; generic state containers can hold its values but cannot adjudicate what each kind must change, when it is a no-op, or what its inverse is.

provenance.attribution: Handcrafted before/mutation/after vector authored against this state lane's own schema; the diff and diagnostics are the production dispatch's, reviewed against the after-snapshot.

fixtureManifests.notes: The owner's committed contract vector for `set-engagement-input` (🧫️fixtures/🔁️mutation-contracts.json), now a fixture bundle of its own.
